framework.name: API & External Service Security Evaluation
framework.description: Deep evaluation of API endpoint security across all FGC services: WhatsApp Bot (port 4100), Attendance Service (port 4201), admin API, contact/subscribe endpoints, and Paystack giving integration. Covers authentication, authorization, rate limiting, input validation, and external service integration patterns.

rubric.1-2: Critical: APIs are exploitable. Unauthenticated access to sensitive operations.
rubric.3-4: Poor: Major gaps in API protection. Multiple endpoints vulnerable.
rubric.5-6: Fair: Basic protections exist but inconsistent across services.
rubric.7-8: Good: Comprehensive API security with minor gaps.
rubric.9-10: Excellent: Defense in depth across all API surfaces.

criteria.name: Complete Endpoint Map
what_to_check: Document EVERY route across all Express apps with: path, method, auth requirement, rate limit, input validation
Classify each endpoint: public, authenticated, admin-only
Check for hidden/debug endpoints that should be removed in production
Verify no Express route wildcards that could match unintended paths
Map which service each endpoint belongs to (bot, attendance, frontend API)
criteria.remediation: Create an API inventory document. Use express-list-endpoints or manual grep of app.get/post/put/delete patterns. Remove any debug/test endpoints.

criteria.name: API Versioning
what_to_check: API routes are versioned (/api/v1/) or have a versioning strategy
Breaking changes don't affect existing consumers
Frontend API utility files reference consistent base URLs
criteria.remediation: Add /api/v1/ prefix to all API routes. Plan for versioning strategy.

criteria.name: Webhook Security
what_to_check: GET /webhook verifies Meta's hub.verify_token challenge correctly
POST /webhook validates X-Hub-Signature-256 header using app secret
Signature validation happens BEFORE any message processing
Invalid signatures return 403/401 and are logged
Webhook endpoint doesn't process duplicate messages (deduplication by message ID)
criteria.remediation: Implement signature verification middleware: crypto.createHmac('sha256', appSecret).update(rawBody).digest('hex') compared to header value. Process raw body before JSON parsing for accurate signature verification.

criteria.name: Outbound Message Security
what_to_check: WhatsApp API token is not logged or exposed in error responses
Outbound messages go through BullMQ queue (not synchronous, preventing webhook timeout)
Failed message sends are retried with backoff (not infinite retries)
Message content is sanitized before sending (no injection into WhatsApp template variables)
Rate limiting respects Meta's messaging limits (1000 messages/24h for unverified business)
criteria.remediation: Ensure token is only in env vars. Configure BullMQ retry with exponential backoff. Track message sending rate against Meta limits.

criteria.name: Inbound Message Processing
what_to_check: Message type is validated (text, image, button response, etc.)
Text messages are length-limited before processing
Command parsing is strict (can't trigger unintended code paths)
FAQ bot responses don't leak internal data
Prayer request intake sanitizes and length-limits content
criteria.remediation: Add type guards for message types. Limit text processing to 1000 chars. Strict command regex patterns.

criteria.name: Check-In Endpoint Security
what_to_check: Self check-in validates member identity (how? phone number? code?)
Assisted check-in requires admin authentication
QR scan check-in validates QR token is current and not reused
Duplicate check-in detection is server-side (not client-side only)
Session auto-generation (Sunday 12AM-6PM) is timezone-safe (Africa/Lagos)
criteria.remediation: Ensure all check-in modes verify identity server-side. QR tokens should be time-limited. Duplicate detection must be atomic (DB constraint).

criteria.name: Data Sync Security
what_to_check: Attendance data sync to bot's PostgreSQL uses authenticated connection
Sync doesn't expose member data in transit between services
Historical attendance data access requires admin auth
criteria.remediation: Secure inter-service communication. Consider shared secret or internal API key for service-to-service calls.

criteria.name: Admin Route Protection
what_to_check: Every /admin or admin-level route requires session token verification
Token verification is middleware (applied before route handler, not inside it)
Admin actions are logged to audit trail (who did what, when)
Super_admin exclusive actions (user management, role changes) have additional checks
Admin API returns minimal data (no excessive data exposure)
criteria.remediation: Apply auth middleware to router-level, not per-route. Log all admin actions. Implement principle of least privilege per role.

criteria.name: Data Management Endpoints
what_to_check: CRUD endpoints for events, members, blog, testimonies, media all require auth
Bulk operations (mass message, bulk attendance) have additional confirmation/logging
Delete operations are soft-delete or have undo capability
Export/download endpoints don't expose more data than intended
criteria.remediation: Audit all CRUD routes. Add confirmation for destructive actions. Implement soft delete.

criteria.name: Contact & Subscribe Endpoints
what_to_check: Contact form endpoint validates email, name, message
Subscribe endpoint validates email format
Both have rate limiting to prevent spam
CAPTCHA or honeypot field for bot prevention
Email injection prevention (no newlines in email/name fields that could inject headers)
Response doesn't confirm if email already exists (prevents enumeration)
known_issues: Rate limiting exists on /api/giving/initialize (10 req/min/IP) — verify contact form and newsletter subscribe endpoints have equivalent protection
criteria.remediation: Add rate limiting (3 submissions per hour per IP). Add honeypot field. Validate and sanitize all fields. Strip newlines from header-bound fields.

criteria.name: Public Data Endpoints
what_to_check: Event listing API only returns public event data (no internal notes/admin fields)
Blog/testimony listing doesn't expose draft/unpublished content
No sensitive data in public API responses (no member phone numbers, etc.)
Pagination is implemented to prevent data dump attacks
criteria.remediation: Audit all public endpoint responses. Use select/projection to return only public fields. Implement pagination with max page size.

categories.name: Payment Integration (Paystack — Live)
categories.description: Paystack is implemented with HMAC-SHA512 webhook validation, transaction state machine, and PostgreSQL storage (giving_transactions table). Evaluate the live implementation.

criteria.name: Payment Security Architecture
what_to_check: Paystack secret key (PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY) is server-side ONLY (never in frontend bundle, not in any VITE_ var)
Paystack public key is used client-side for Paystack Popup/Inline payment
Webhook endpoint verifies Paystack signature (X-Paystack-Signature header) using HMAC-SHA512
Payment amounts are validated server-side (user can't modify amount client-side)
Idempotency: duplicate webhook events don't create duplicate records (transaction state machine prevents this)
Test vs Live key separation by environment
Webhook timestamp validation rejects events older than 5 minutes (configurable via WEBHOOK_MAX_AGE_MS)
criteria.remediation: Use Paystack's recommended architecture: client collects payment via Popup/Inline, server verifies via webhook. Never trust client-reported payment amounts.

criteria.name: Payment Data Handling
what_to_check: No card numbers stored in your database (Paystack handles PCI compliance)
Transaction references are unique and unpredictable
Payment logs don't contain full card details
Giving/tithe records are access-controlled (who can see who donated)
Payment failure handling doesn't leak error details to user
Giving admin dashboard masks donor PII (name, email, phone) for non-super_admin roles — verify masking is effective and cannot be bypassed via API
criteria.remediation: Store only transaction references and Paystack-provided metadata. Implement access controls on giving records. Log transaction events without sensitive data.

criteria.name: Bot Notification Bridge Security
what_to_check: /bot/api/giving/notify endpoint requires BOT_ADMIN_API_KEY header authentication
Endpoint cannot be used to send arbitrary WhatsApp messages (only sends pre-defined thank-you template)
Fire-and-forget pattern from website API to bot does not silently drop failures — verify error logging exists
Thank-you message respects opt-out status (does not message opted-out phone numbers)
Notification payload is validated (phone number format, transaction reference exists in DB)
Donor PII (name, email, amount) is not leaked in server logs when notification is processed
known_issues: Phase 3 added /bot/api/giving/notify as internal endpoint — verify BOT_ADMIN_API_KEY check is present and correct
Fire-and-forget from website to bot may silently drop failures — verify error logging
criteria.remediation: Verify BOT_ADMIN_API_KEY middleware. Check opt-out before sending. Log failures with transaction ref but not PII. Validate notification payload schema.

criteria.name: LLM Provider Security
what_to_check: API keys for Vertex AI, OpenAI, Gemini are env-var only
Cascading fallback (Vertex -> OpenAI -> Gemini -> static) handles failures gracefully
LLM API errors don't leak API keys or provider details to users
Request timeouts are set (LLM calls can hang)
Cost controls: message generation is rate-limited to prevent runaway API costs
criteria.remediation: Set timeouts on all LLM API calls (10-30s). Implement per-day/per-hour cost caps. Log provider usage for cost tracking.

criteria.name: Prompt Injection Prevention
what_to_check: User-provided content (names, prayer requests, feedback) passed to LLM is treated as data, not instructions
System prompts clearly delineate user content from instructions
LLM output is validated/filtered before being used (sent as WhatsApp message, stored in DB)
No user input directly concatenated into system prompts
criteria.remediation: Use message role separation (system vs user). Wrap user content in delimiters. Validate LLM output against expected format before use.

evaluation_instructions.for_claude_code: Evaluate by: 1) Map all Express routes across all services (grep -r 'app.get\|app.post\|app.put\|app.delete\|router.get\|router.post' --include='*.js' --include='*.ts'), 2) For each route, check auth middleware, validation, rate limiting, 3) Test webhook verification logic, 4) Review all API utility files in frontend (src/utils/*Api.js), 5) Score each criterion with file:line evidence.
